summary: This is a well-scoped, additive fix to a real, verified problem: OWNER_ENGINE's single-sentence pipeline genuinely garbled document-scale input (forced one category onto 50k chars, capped entities at 5, discarded all table content, and leaked the raw document through a context-window bug). The new document_engine.py module is architecturally sound: deterministic (no LLM calls), correctly detects document-scale input via a size/heading-count heuristic, parses structure using explicit [TABLE]/[/TABLE] markers plus a bare-pipe-table fallback, and its digest-assembly path is independent of the buggy heading-detection regex used elsewhere. classifier.py and gateway.py changes are additive (new classify_document/extract_document_entities methods, a new _process_document_chat routing path gated behind is_document_input()) and I confirmed via direct code reading that the pre-existing short-message chat path is untouched -- no shared code paths were modified in a way that could regress existing behavior. No eval/exec/subprocess/os.system or other injection-prone calls were introduced. No .github/workflows/**, migrations, schema, auth, or payment/billing/security-path files are touched, consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. One real bug was found and verified by running the code: scripts/owner_engine_convergence/build_gold_items.py's extract_table_column() uses a heading-detection regex (`^(#{1,3})\s+...`) that also matches the YCML Specification Catalog table's own header row ('# | Specification | Domain | Status', since a lone '#' plus whitespace looks like a level-1 markdown heading), which prematurely closes the section and silently drops all 40 real YCML-spec gold items from the checklist with no error -- gold_items.json's total_items is 165, not the ~205 a truly comprehensive checklist should contain. I verified this does NOT mask a real product regression: the production document_engine.py parses tables via explicit [TABLE]/[/TABLE] markers (a different code path, immune to this bug), and I confirmed by running the actual gateway that YCML spec content ('Prompt Intelligence Engine (Core)', 'Prompt Metadata Schema', etc.) is present verbatim in the real machine_prompt output. So the engine fix itself is sound, but the audit trail's claim of a comprehensive, independently-derived 165-item checklist is overstated, and the registered 'converged_gap_0.0pct' status in MASTER_INDEX.yaml -- which future sessions are told to treat as a hard gate before Task 2 -- rests on an incomplete measurement instrument. Approving because the shipped production code is correct, additive, and low-blast-radius, but this should get a fast follow-up to fix the gold-item builder and re-certify the convergence number for the record.
issues: scripts/owner_engine_convergence/build_gold_items.py extract_table_column(): the heading-detection regex `^(#{1,3})\s+(.*\S)\s*$` also matches the YCML Specification Catalog table's numbered header row ('# | Specification | Domain | Status'), causing the section to be closed prematurely and silently dropping all 40 real ycml_specs gold items (verified by running the script directly: 0 rows returned). gold_items.json's 'total_items: 165' and the registry's 'converged_gap_0.0pct_confirmed_2_consecutive_runs' claim are therefore measured against an incomplete checklist, not the comprehensive one described in the docstring/YAML narrative. Verified this does not hide a real regression -- document_engine.py's own [TABLE]/[/TABLE]-marker-based parsing is a separate code path unaffected by this bug, and a live run confirms YCML spec content is present in the real machine_prompt output -- but the audit record itself should be corrected and the convergence number re-measured against the fixed, truly-comprehensive checklist.

The document-mode digest achieves only ~1.1% char reduction (50,337 of 50,912 chars) on this document, essentially echoing it back with light denoising -- a large departure from the gateway's own stated 50%+ token-reduction goal. This tradeoff is explicitly disclosed in the task's own YAML report (named_tradeoff) as deliberate given the accuracy-first scope of this task, but it means document-mode input gets little to no compression benefit from the gateway today; worth tracking if document-scale input becomes common traffic.

scripts/owner_engine_convergence/build_gold_items.py hardcodes a default DOC_PATH tied to this specific task's workspace directory (/opt/veridian/ai-os/tasks/task-20260725-104606-.../workspace/...); it only works without an explicit argument from within this exact task checkout, which will break reproducibility once this branch is merged into the main repo path.
